newsitem.title: UK: EMU stability council no threat to ECB - Juppe.
newsitem.headline: EMU stability council no threat to ECB - Juppe.

text.p: A proposed stability council to coordinate economic policy inside the single-currency zone would not undermine the independence of the future European central bank (ECB), French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday.
Speaking to reporters after talks at Downing Street with British Prime Minister John Major, Juppe said the independence of the ECB would be respected.

"But it is also absolutely necessary to have cooperation and dialogue between the countries which will participate in EMU, and the council of stability and growth is the place where this cooperation must stake place," Juppe, speaking in English, said.
Juppe said of the proposed council: "It is in the spirit of the Maastricht treaty, and there is no question of stopping the independence of the central bank in such a project."
The French prime minister said he hoped Britain would join economic and monetary union when it is launched in 1999 or later. France, for its part, would meet the stiff convergence criteria, he added.

"We also believe it would be in the interest of all our partners, and especially of Great Britain, to join us... I wish that either in the first wave or second wave Great Britain will join us," Juppe said.
Major, whose government has the right to opt out of EMU, repeated his doubts as to whether the single currency would go ahead on schedule in 1999.
"There is a difference of view between our European partners and us upon that -- about whether the convergence criteria will be clearly sustainable at that particular date.
"The importance of the economic criteria are such that if it isn't sustainable we are very dubious about the desirability of its proceeding," Major said.
